chapters.name: Heads pass notes
chapters.note: where does the earlier head's note go in?

cap.1: One attention head can only look and copy. The clever tricks happen when a later head reads what an earlier head wrote. But where does that note go in?
cap.2: Every head reads the residual stream and writes back into it, so a later head can use an earlier head's output as input to its queries, keys or values. That is composition.
cap.3: Heads communicate only through the residual stream: a later head's W_Q, W_K or W_V can read a subspace an earlier head's W_OV writes to. Q-, K- or V-composition (Elhage et al., 2021).

cap.1: A shopper walks past labelled stalls with a list. Q-composition is an earlier helper adding a line to it. The stalls stay the same; what you look for changes.
cap.2: The later head's query is computed from the residual stream at its own position, and that stream already holds the earlier head's output. So the earlier head edits the search.
cap.3: Q-composition: the sender's W_OV writes into the destination residual stream in a subspace the receiver's W_Q reads, changing its attention scores from the query side.

cap.1: An earlier head's note can land in three places: the later head's list (Q), the stall labels (K) or the shopping bags (V). This film is about the list.
cap.2: Q-composition changes what the later head looks for. K-composition changes how the positions it looks at are described. V-composition changes what it carries away.
cap.3: Q- and K-composition both alter the attention pattern (the QK circuit), from the destination or the source side; V-composition alters what is moved (the OV circuit).

cap.1: In the IOI sentence, John appears twice. Helper heads write 'not John' on the name mover's list, so it looks at Mary and copies her name out.
cap.2: In IOI, S-inhibition heads (7.3, 7.9, 8.6, 8.10) carry a 'John is duplicated' signal to the final position. It enters the name movers' queries, so they avoid John and copy Mary.
cap.3: Wang et al. (2022): the S-inhibition signal enters name movers 9.6, 9.9 and 10.0 through their queries rather than their keys, suppressing attention to S; path patching establishes it.

chapters.name: Which door?

left.title: patch the head's whole input
lines: changes Q, K and V at once

right.title: patch only the path into Q
lines: edits just what reaches the query
choice flips: it was the list

chapters.verdict: To prove Q-composition, patch the path into the queries.

cap.1: Knowing a note mattered is not the same as knowing it went on the list. To prove it, change only what reaches the list and see if the choice changes.
cap.2: Activation patching a head's input changes its queries, keys and values together. Path patching the S-inhibition output into only the name movers' queries shows it is Q-composition.
cap.3: 'Q, not K' is a claim about a path: sender W_OV into receiver W_Q. Path patching into the queries alone, or weights-based composition scores, isolates it; plain activation patching cannot.

cap.1: Circuits are heads passing notes. Knowing where each note goes (the list, the labels or the bags) is how you read a model's reasoning step by step.
cap.2: When you trace a circuit, ask of every link: did the earlier head change the query, the key or the value? For S-inhibition into name movers, the answer is the query.
cap.3: To ablate or steer a sender with intent, you need its receiver's input channel; Q-composition says the effect flows through the receiver's attention, on the query side.

coda.title: A toy name mover: Mary or John?

params.label: how much the query reads the note

readouts.label: attention on Mary at this note strength

caption.1: Slide the note strength and watch attention swing from John to Mary. Then set 'reads the note' to 0: the note is still written, but the query never sees it.
caption.2: A toy name mover: John starts with a head start, and the note in the query subtracts from John's score. Reading strength 0 means W_Q ignores the subspace the note is in.
caption.3: Two-way softmax: p(Mary) = σ(g·s − b). g stands in for the overlap between the sender's W_OV output and the receiver's W_Q input, which composition scores measure. Toy numbers.

where_else: K-composition in induction heads: there the earlier head relabels the keys instead
Query rewriting in search and retrieval: an earlier step edits what the next lookup asks for
Circuit tracing in general: every head-to-head link is Q, K or V composition

hamming.what: A later attention head building its query partly from an earlier head's output, so the earlier head changes what the later head looks for.
hamming.when: When tracing circuits such as IOI, where S-inhibition heads steer the name movers away from the repeated name.
hamming.why: It is one of only three ways heads can cooperate, and knowing which door a signal uses tells you how to test, ablate or steer it.

object.title: The rewritten list
object.subtitle: The IOI hand-off in space: a note from the S-inhibition heads enters the name mover through its query, never its keys.

nodes.label: residual stream at the final token

cap.1: The helper heads write a note, 'John is the repeat', into the stream at the last word of the sentence.
cap.2: S-inhibition heads move the duplicated-name signal from the second John to the final position.
cap.3: S-inhibition heads V-compose the duplicate flag from S2 and write it into the END residual stream.

cap.1: The name mover builds its question from that same stream, so the note lands right on its shopping list.
cap.2: The name mover's query is read from the END stream, so the inhibition signal becomes part of what it searches for.
cap.3: Q-composition: the receiver's W_Q reads the subspace the senders' W_OV wrote at the destination position.

cap.1: The keys at Mary and John are left alone. The stalls did not change; the shopper's list did.
cap.2: Keys at the name positions are not the channel here; that would be K-composition, a different door.
cap.3: Per Wang et al. (2022) the effect enters via queries rather than keys, which path patching distinguishes.

cap.1: With 'not John' on its list, the name mover attends to Mary and copies her name into the answer.
cap.2: Attention shifts to the indirect object, and the name mover's OV circuit copies Mary into the logits.
cap.3: Name movers attend END to IO and write it to the logits through their OV circuits, raising logit[IO] − logit[S].

predict.q: In Q-composition, which input of the later head does the earlier head change?

options.t: Its query: what it looks for
Its keys: how positions are labelled

predict.why: Q-composition writes into the subspace the later head's W_Q reads at the destination. Keys and values are the other two doors.

predict.q: How do you show the S-inhibition signal enters name movers through queries, not keys?

options.t: Path patching into the queries only
Look at the name movers' attention pattern

predict.why: Only patching the sender-to-query path isolates the door; patterns and ablations cannot tell Q from K.

predict.q: Q- and K-composition both change the later head's...
predict.why: Both feed the QK side, so they redirect attention. V-composition feeds the OV side and changes what is moved.

object.where: Any pipeline where one step rewrites the next step's search, like query rewriting before retrieval.
